title: Knowledge Check 5 - Lessons 21-25
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 21-25 - Practical Application of Agentforce Sales Expertise. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A validation rule references a field the running user cannot see because of field-level security. What happens on save?
options: The rule is skipped for that user
The rule evaluates normally because validation formulas ignore field-level security
The save errors out with a permissions message
The restricted field becomes visible to the user
questions.explanation: Field-level security governs visibility and edit access, not formula evaluation, so the validation rule still reads the field and evaluates normally.

questions.question: In the save order of execution, which of these runs first?
options: Before-save record-triggered Flow
Custom validation rules
After Apex triggers
After-save record-triggered Flow
questions.explanation: Before-save Flows run before validation rules and before triggers, which is exactly why they cannot be used to evade a validation rule.

questions.question: Which requirement forces you off declarative configuration and onto Apex?
options: A field update when a record is created
A page layout that differs by profile
Bulk processing of two hundred thousand records with complex logic that risks governor limits
Sending an email when a field changes
questions.explanation: Large-volume bulk processing with complex logic and tight governor-limit control is a named boundary where Flow's limits force Apex, while the other options are routine declarative work.

questions.question: You must process five hundred thousand records nightly with complex amount recalculation and tight governor-limit control. What do you build?
options: A record-triggered Flow
A screen Flow launched from a list button
A batch Apex class scheduled nightly
A validation rule with a formula
questions.explanation: Large-volume nightly processing with complex logic and governor-limit control is a named Apex boundary that a Flow's limits cannot meet.

questions.question: A managed package installed in your org is consuming your CPU governor limits. What is true?
options: Managed package Apex runs in an isolated limits context
Apex in managed packages still counts against your org's governor limits
You can edit the package's Apex to reduce its consumption
Governor limits apply only to your own Apex
questions.explanation: Packaged Apex executes inside your org against your limits, and because package components are locked you cannot edit it to reduce consumption.

questions.question: Which email integration syncs email and events into a separate activity store rather than as reportable EmailMessage records?
options: Einstein Activity Capture
Email-to-Case
Web-to-Lead
Case auto-response rules
questions.explanation: Einstein Activity Capture syncs Gmail and Outlook email and events into a separate activity store, which is why those activities are not fully reportable as EmailMessage records.

questions.question: The Opportunity OWD is Private and a sales manager's role sits above the reps. What does the manager see?
options: Nothing, because Private hides the records from everyone but the owner
The manager sees the reps' opportunities through the role hierarchy
The manager must be added to each opportunity's team
Only opportunities the manager owns
questions.explanation: A Private OWD restricts to the owner and users above them in the role hierarchy, so the manager sees the reports' records without a team or sharing rule.

questions.question: Can a sharing rule remove access from a group that already has it?
options: Yes, if the rule is criteria-based
Only on custom objects
No, because sharing rules only extend the access the OWD and role hierarchy provide
Yes, when the target is a public group
questions.explanation: Sharing rules are additive only, so removing access requires a change to the OWD, object permissions, or field-level security rather than a sharing rule.

questions.question: Which configuration makes contact visibility follow the account's sharing?
options: Controlled by Parent as the Contact organization-wide default
Public Read Only on Contact
A criteria-based Contact sharing rule
Grant Access Using Hierarchies cleared on Contact
questions.explanation: Setting the Contact OWD to Controlled by Parent makes contacts inherit their account's access, so no separate contact sharing model is needed.

questions.question: Two users share a role, but one needs two extra field permissions. What is the recommended fix?
options: Create a second profile with those field permissions
Assign a permission set that grants the extra access to the one user
Change the organization-wide default
Add the user to a sharing rule
questions.explanation: Permission sets are the additive, maintainable way to grant a single user extra access, while a second profile is one-per-user overhead and sharing does not control field permissions.

questions.question: You muted Read on an object in a permission set group's muting permission set. What else is muted?
options: Only Read is muted
Read and nothing else in the group
Create, Edit, Delete, View All Records, and Modify All Records
Only Modify All Records
questions.explanation: Muting cascades through permission dependencies, and because Create, Edit, Delete, View All, and Modify All are unusable without read, they are muted along with it.

questions.question: A user must collaborate on one deal while the rest of the account stays hidden. What do you configure?
options: An Opportunity Team membership for that opportunity
An Account Team membership
A change to the user's role
A change to the organization-wide default
questions.explanation: An Opportunity Team grants access to that opportunity only, which fits a deal-specific need, whereas an Account Team and an OWD change would open the whole account.

questions.question: On which object is the price of a product for one specific price book actually stored?
options: Product2
PricebookEntry
Pricebook2
OpportunityLineItem
questions.explanation: The PricebookEntry joins one product to one price book and holds the UnitPrice, which is why a product record has no price field of its own and a product has one entry per price book.

questions.question: An opportunity line has a quantity of ten, a sales price of two hundred dollars, and a ten percent discount. What does Total Price equal?
options: Quantity times List Price
Quantity times Sales Price plus the discount
Quantity times Sales Price times one minus the discount
The standard price book UnitPrice for the product
questions.explanation: Total Price is Quantity times Sales Price times one minus the discount, giving one thousand eight hundred dollars here, and that figure is what rolls into the opportunity Amount.

questions.question: Before a product can be added to any custom price book or to an opportunity, it must have an entry in which price book?
options: Any active custom price book in the org
The price book set on the opportunity
The corporate currency price book
The standard price book
questions.explanation: The standard price book entry is mandatory first, because custom price book entries and opportunity line items derive from it, so an answer that skips the standard book is wrong.
